You are an adversarial verifier for a proposed STRUCTURAL refactor in the andesim repo at /home/nick/work/andesim.
READ-ONLY: do not edit, build, or run anything. Use Read/Grep/Glob only.

Claim (from reviewer driver-run):
- file: driver/cmd_run.cpp:528
- category: dead-code
- title: --print-memmap 'OVERLAPS the reserved V-scratch page' branch is unreachable
- detail: In run_hybrid, the L26/F3 overlap guard (cmd_run.cpp:468-483) runs unconditionally, including in memmap_only mode: it computes scratch_gpa = physical_mmap_bytes(mem) - HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES, which equals mem exactly (shm.cpp:87-89 defines physical_mmap_bytes as program_bytes + HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES), and returns fail() when elf_load_top(elf_path) > scratch_gpa. The --print-memmap block at lines 504-532 executes only after that guard passed, and calls the same deterministic elf_load_top on the same elf_path, so at line 526 'top <= mem' is always true and the else-branch string 'OVERLAPS the reserved V-scratch page; raise --mem-size' (lines 528-529) can never print. Note the design tension: the comment at lines 403-406 says the ELF 'only adds the fit-vs-scratch note' in memmap mode, but the hard guard fires first - if the OVERLAPS note was meant to be reachable under --print-memmap, the guard would need a memmap_only skip (a behavioral choice, out of structural scope).
- claimed safety: Removing the unreachable ternary else-branch (leaving the unconditional 'fits DRAM' note, or hoisting the guard result) cannot change any observable output, because no input reaches that branch: any ELF with top > mem already exited with the fail() diagnostic before the memmap block runs.

Try to REFUTE it. For dead-code: grep the WHOLE repo (and the demo suite at /home/nick/work/andesim-demo, and consider that vsim lives in a separate repo /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim - grep there too if the symbol could cross repos) for references. For duplication: read both sites fully and check they really are behavior-identical. For stale-doc: read the doc AND the code it describes. For bug-report: check whether the behavior is actually wrong vs intended. If the change could alter ANY observable behavior (output text, exit codes, file layout, test expectations), verdict RISKY with the exact risk. If the claim is wrong, REJECTED. Only CONFIRMED when you verified the evidence yourself.

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# --print-memmap: `andesim run --mode hybrid --print-memmap` prints the
3	# hybrid-SUPPORTED guest memory map (DRAM window sized by --mem-size, the
4	# reserved V-scratch page, backdoor-gated ILM/DLM/HVM rows with bases from the
5	# engine's --print-qemu-config, SimControl/HTIF, UART2) and exits 0 without
6	# spawning a simulation. Unsupported regions (QEMU-only devices, PLDM, ...)
7	# must NOT appear.
8	#
9	# Three layers:
10	#   1. unit (fast, always runs): the composer's own tests
11	#      (build/driver/andesim-memmap-test).
12	#   2. driver behavior (needs a built vsim engine; SKIPs otherwise): the
13	#      printed rows track --mem-size and the engine's --describe sizes.
14	#   3. engine contract (same engine): the driver's platform-constant rows and
15	#      LM/HVM bases appear in the engine's OWN `--print-memmap` interconnect
16	#      dump -- the closed loop that catches driver/vsim drift.
17	set -uo pipefail
18	
19	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
20	ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
21	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
22	
23	# 1. unit: the pure composer
24	bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
25	BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
26	[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing driver binary: $BIN"
27	UNIT="$ROOT/build/driver/andesim-memmap-test"
28	[ -x "$UNIT" ] || fail "missing unit-test binary: $UNIT"
29	"$UNIT" >/dev/null || fail "memmap unit tests failed"
30	ok "unit: hybrid memmap composer"
31	
32	# Mode gating needs no engine: the map is hybrid-only surface.
33	expect 2 'requires --mode hybrid' "$BIN" run --mode fast --print-memmap
34	expect 2 'requires --mode hybrid' "$BIN" run --mode cycle --print-memmap
35	ok "gating: --print-memmap rejects fast/cycle"
36	
37	# 2 + 3 need a built vsim engine. Resolve like the driver does.
38	BINDIR=$(vsim_bin_dir)
39	SIM=$(ls "$BINDIR"/sim_* 2>/dev/null | head -1)
40	if [ -z "$SIM" ] || [ ! -x "$SIM" ]; then
41	  ok "SKIP driver/engine layers: no built vsim engine under $BINDIR (set VSIM_BIN_DIR)"
42	  exit 0
43	fi
44	base=$(basename "$SIM"); base=${base#sim_}
45	id="vsim:${base}"
46	
47	# 2. driver behavior. No ELF required: the map describes the run's window,
48	# not a workload.
49	out=$(VSIM_BIN_DIR="$BINDIR" "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --print-memmap \
50	      --engine "$id" 2>&1); rc=$?
51	[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "--print-memmap exit $rc: $out"
52	printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q '^DRAM .*0x7ffffff ' \
53	  || fail "DRAM row missing/incorrect for the 128M default: $out"
54	printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q '^V-scratch .*0x8000000 .*0x8000fff ' \
55	  || fail "V-scratch row missing/incorrect: $out"
56	printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q '^SimControl/HTIF .*0xe0080000 ' \
57	  || fail "SimControl row missing: $out"
58	printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q '^UART2 .*0xf0300000 ' \
59	  || fail "UART2 row missing: $out"
60	# Unsupported regions must not leak in.
61	printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qi 'PLDM\|PLIC\|UART1\|SMU' \
62	  && fail "unsupported region leaked into the map: $out"
63	ok "driver: DRAM/V-scratch/device rows for the 128M default"
64	
65	# --mem-size moves the DRAM top and the scratch page together.
66	out64=$(VSIM_BIN_DIR="$BINDIR" "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --print-memmap \
67	        --engine "$id" --mem-size 64M 2>&1); rc=$?
68	[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "--print-memmap --mem-size 64M exit $rc: $out64"
69	printf '%s\n' "$out64" | grep -q '^DRAM .*0x3ffffff ' \
70	  || fail "DRAM row does not track --mem-size 64M: $out64"
71	printf '%s\n' "$out64" | grep -q '^V-scratch .*0x4000000 ' \
72	  || fail "V-scratch row does not track --mem-size 64M: $out64"
73	ok "driver: rows track --mem-size"
74	
75	# LM rows follow the engine's --describe (backdoor-gated): present iff size>0.
76	desc=$("$SIM" --describe 2>/dev/null)
77	d_int() { printf '%s' "$desc" | tr -d ' \n' | grep -o "\"$1\":[0-9]*" | grep -o '[0-9]*$'; }
78	ilm=$(d_int ilm_size); dlm=$(d_int dlm_size); hvm=$(d_int hvm_size)
79	for pair in "ILM:${ilm:-0}" "DLM:${dlm:-0}" "HVM:${hvm:-0}"; do
80	  region=${pair%%:*}; size=${pair##*:}
81	  if [ "$size" -gt 0 ]; then
82	    printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q "^$region " \
83	      || fail "$region row missing though --describe size=$size: $out"
84	  else
85	    printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q "^$region " \
86	      && fail "$region row present though --describe size=0: $out"
87	  fi
88	done
89	ok "driver: ILM/DLM/HVM rows follow --describe sizes (ilm=${ilm:-0} dlm=${dlm:-0} hvm=${hvm:-0})"
90	
91	# 3. engine contract: the closed loop. Every platform base the driver prints
92	# must be decoded by the engine's own interconnect (its --print-memmap), and
93	# the LM/HVM bases the driver took from --print-qemu-config must appear too.
94	# Base-only match: the engine dump's sizes carry a known +1 display bug (and
95	# a 4x HVM aperture bug) until the vsim-side fixes land.
96	edump=$("$SIM" --print-memmap 2>&1) || fail "engine --print-memmap failed: $edump"
97	for b in 0xe0080000 0xf0300000; do
98	  printf '%s\n' "$edump" | grep -q "\[$b-" \
99	    || fail "engine dump missing platform base $b: $edump"
100	done
101	if [ "${hvm:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
102	  hvm_base=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk '/^HVM /{print $2}')
103	  printf '%s\n' "$edump" | grep -q "\[$hvm_base-" \
104	    || fail "engine dump does not decode the driver's HVM base $hvm_base: $edump"
105	fi
106	ok "engine contract: driver bases appear in $base --print-memmap"
107	
108	echo "PASS test_andes_sim_print_memmap"
109

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Self-asserting harness for the memsize demo.
3	#
4	# This IS the "test framework" for these demos: a program's pass/fail is its
5	# SimControl exit code + stdout marker, and the driver's pass/fail is its own
6	# process exit code. Both are asserted here in portable bash -- no gtest, no
7	# libstdc++ on the target, nothing to cross-compile. Same pattern as andesim's
8	# own tests/andes_sim/*.sh.
9	set -uo pipefail
10	HERE=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
11	cd "$HERE"
12	
13	A=${ANDESIM_BIN:-/home/nick/work/andesim/andesim}
14	ENG=${ENGINE:-vsim:ax45mpv_premium}
15	SUM='0x5e949e00'          # checksum is --mem-size-independent (determinism)
16	
17	pass=0 fail=0
18	# assert DESC WANT_RC WANT_REGEX -- CMD...
19	assert() {
20	  local desc=$1 want_rc=$2 want_re=$3; shift 3
21	  local out rc
22	  out=$("$@" </dev/null 2>&1); rc=$?
23	  if [ "$rc" -eq "$want_rc" ] && grep -qiE "$want_re" <<<"$out"; then
24	    printf '[PASS] %s\n' "$desc"; pass=$((pass+1))
25	  else
26	    printf '[FAIL] %s\n       rc=%s (want %s), no /%s/ in:\n       %s\n' \
27	      "$desc" "$rc" "$want_rc" "$want_re" "$(head -1 <<<"$out")"
28	    fail=$((fail+1))
29	  fi
30	}
31	
32	echo "--- accept + run (checksum is the same at any size) ---"
33	assert "fast  64M  runs, checksum $SUM"  0 "memsize PASS checksum=$SUM" \
34	  "$A" run --mode fast --mem-size 64M  memsize.elf
35	assert "fast  256M runs, same checksum"  0 "memsize PASS checksum=$SUM" \
36	  "$A" run --mode fast --mem-size 256M memsize.elf
37	
38	echo "--- different sizes: hybrid DRAM window tracks --mem-size ---"
39	assert "hybrid 1.5G   -> DRAM 1536M"      0 "DRAM.*1536M" \
40	  "$A" run --mode hybrid --print-memmap --engine "$ENG" --mem-size 1.5G   memsize.elf
41	assert "hybrid 131072K-> DRAM 128M"       0 "DRAM.*128M" \
42	  "$A" run --mode hybrid --print-memmap --engine "$ENG" --mem-size 131072K memsize.elf
43	
44	echo "--- boundary: cap = 2 GiB - one V-scratch page ---"
45	assert "hybrid 2047M accepted (largest)"  0 "2047M" \
46	  "$A" run --mode hybrid --print-memmap --engine "$ENG" --mem-size 2047M memsize.elf
47	assert "hybrid 2G rejected (overflow)"    2 "exceeds the AE350 DRAM window" \
48	  "$A" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENG" --mem-size 2G memsize.elf
49	
50	echo "--- negative: invalid specs rejected before any spawn ---"
51	assert "0   -> must be > 0"                2 "must be > 0" \
52	  "$A" run --mode fast --mem-size 0   memsize.elf
53	assert "-5  -> expected <number>"          2 "expected <number>" \
54	  "$A" run --mode fast --mem-size -5  memsize.elf
55	assert "abc -> expected <number>"          2 "expected <number>" \
56	  "$A" run --mode fast --mem-size abc memsize.elf
57	assert "fast 1000 -> whole MiB rule"       2 "whole MiB" \
58	  "$A" run --mode fast --mem-size 1000 memsize.elf
59	
60	echo "--- fit: --mem-size vs the program's own 64 MiB static footprint ---"
61	assert "big ELF @ 32M rejected"            2 "raise --mem-size" \
62	  "$A" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENG" --mem-size 32M memsize_big.elf
63	assert "big ELF @ 128M fits DRAM"          0 "fits DRAM" \
64	  "$A" run --mode hybrid --print-memmap --engine "$ENG" --mem-size 128M memsize_big.elf
65	
66	echo "-----------------------------------------------------------"
67	printf 'RESULT: %d passed, %d failed\n' "$pass" "$fail"
68	[ "$fail" -eq 0 ]
